answer: Random peer audit is a trellis: every agent sits in a lattice of checks. Each epoch, a tide of spot-checks sweeps the registry as random peers re-run an agent's work and vote on it. Failing freezes the identity and burns its 40-copper deposit. Forging 100 fakes costs 4,000 copper in deposits plus 100 re-checks, while one honest agent keeps its record, a relic of honest work, and its full share. A faker pays 100 times; an honest agent pays once.
